PullRequest.Title: agentHost: don't forward runtime-loaded user instructions as instructionDirectories
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #342394

## Problem

In a Copilot CLI (Agent Host) session, every file in `~/.copilot/instructions` reaches the system prompt twice.

The launcher creates sessions with `enableConfigDiscovery: true`, so the runtime already loads `<COPILOT_HOME>/instructions` itself. Session discovery also reports those rules, `mapToParsedPlugin()` puts them into the synthetic session plugin, and the launcher forwards them to `createSession` as `instructionDirectories`. The runtime does not deduplicate explicit `instructionDirectories` against the user instructions it discovers.

## Change

`mapToParsedPlugin()` takes an optional `isLoadedByRuntime` predicate and skips matching rules. `SessionPluginController._appliedPlugins()` passes a predicate for `<COPILOT_HOME>/instructions` (compared case-insensitively on Windows, via `extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase`). `SessionPluginController` now injects `ICopilotHomeService`.

Only the SDK config changes. The discovered rules are still listed and published as customizations.

## Why not drop all discovered instructions (`instructions: []`)?

I measured the runtime behaviour with `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.23-preview.5 (the version on `main`), an isolated `COPILOT_HOME`, and `enableConfigDiscovery: true`. I counted a marker heading in the `system.message` event:

| `instructionDirectories` | `<COPILOT_HOME>/instructions` | primary workspace `.github/instructions` | additional folder (`additionalDirectories`) `.github/instructions` |
|---|---|---|---|
| not set | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| the same directory, passed explicitly | **2** | 1 (also for lower-case drive letter and `/` separators) | 1 |

- Only the user-level directory is duplicated. The primary workspace is not, even with path spelling variants.
- The runtime does not discover instructions for additional multi-root folders on its own, so the explicit directories are what make those folders work. Dropping all discovered instructions would regress multi-root workspaces, so only the user-level directory is skipped.

## Tests

- New `CopilotAgent` test: user-level and workspace instructions are both discovered, and the launch config contains only the workspace directory. It fails without the change (`\mock-home\.copilot\instructions` is passed) and passes with it.
- `copilotAgent.test.ts`: 857 passing, 0 failing. `copilotPluginConverters.test.ts` also passes.
- `eslint` is clean on the changed files. The only type errors in `agentHost` come from the missing `electron` types in my environment.
- I did not run VS Code itself with this change. The end-to-end behaviour was checked at the SDK level, as above.

## Not covered

- Other discovered locations that are not under `<COPILOT_HOME>/instructions` are unchanged. The primary-workspace case did not duplicate in my measurement.
- `skillDirectories` is built the same way from discovered skills. I did not check whether it has a similar issue.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each launched or resumed chat session passed the Copilot-home instruction directory explicitly while SDK config discovery independently loaded it, duplicating filesystem loading and retaining/serializing the same instruction text twice in the model system prompt. Cost scaled with total user-instruction bytes and with sessions/turns that carry the prompt.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: User instruction content appeared twice in the system message, consuming duplicate prompt bytes/tokens and increasing model-request latency and context usage for sessions with user instructions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Session plugin projection now excludes rules beneath the runtime-owned <COPILOT_HOME>/instructions directory, while retaining workspace and additional-root instruction directories. The SDK therefore performs only its native user-instruction load instead of also receiving the same directory explicitly.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: At the blamed base line, _appliedPlugins projected every discovered rule into the synthetic session plugin. copilotSessionLauncher.ts then flattens those instructions through toSdkInstructionDirectories and passes the resulting directories to createSession while enableConfigDiscovery is true. The changed test exercises the real warm-chat launch path and proves that the Copilot-home directory previously reached instructionDirectories alongside the workspace directory; the added predicate removes only rules under <COPILOT_HOME>/instructions. The changed code and PR's measured system.message behavior establish that the runtime also discovers this user directory, so the old launch loaded the same user instruction content twice.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, warm, or resume a Copilot Agent Host chat with user-level and workspace instruction files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session snapshot waits for host/client customization sync and anchor discovery, projects enabled plugins, converts projected rules to instructionDirectories, and then calls the SDK create/resume path. Runtime config discovery and explicit instruction-directory loading must complete before the session's system prompt is usable; subsequent model requests carry that prompt on their network critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and parse instruction files for the session's anchor directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery state per shared anchor set, covering the Copilot-home root and workspace roots; watcher bursts are coalesced and the resulting customizations are retained in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host performed the same customization discovery and caching before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial discovery is awaited before the plugin snapshot used for launch; later unchanged snapshots reuse observed discovery state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The SDK runtime discovers config and loads explicitly supplied instruction directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After directory deduplication, normally one Copilot-home instruction root plus one root per relevant workspace grouping. The diff removes the explicit Copilot-home root, leaving the runtime's single native load and preserving workspace/additional-root loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With enableConfigDiscovery true, the runtime loaded the Copilot-home instructions natively and also received that same root through instructionDirectories, so each user instruction was loaded twice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Instruction loading contributes to session/system-prompt initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and carry instruction text in the system prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, total user-instruction bytes were represented twice; after the diff they are represented once. Workspace instructions retain their previous single representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Duplicate user instructions increased prompt allocation, serialization, network payload/context usage, and model processing on sessions using those files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: System-prompt construction precedes useful model interaction, and prompt bytes/tokens are carried on model requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with total bytes and file count under <COPILOT_HOME>/instructions and with the number of independently launched/resumed sessions and model turns carrying the system prompt; effective directory cardinality is one user root after the fix, plus preserved workspace/additional roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host sync, client syncs, discovered customization settling, and MCP refresh are awaited with Promise.all. Directory paths are deduplicated by toSdkResourceDirectories, but user-level runtime discovery and explicit loading were independent rather than coalesced. Sessions launch independently, with no cross-session coalescing evidenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionDiscoveredEntry retains parsed discovery results per shared anchor and avoids unchanged refresh publication. Directory conversion deduplicates identical parent paths within a snapshot. The SDK's per-session native config discovery remains; the change removes the redundant explicit user-root source rather than adding a cache. Cold sessions avoid one duplicate user-root load, and no changed warm-cache invalidation or negative-cache behavior was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path from projected rules to instructionDirectories and enableConfigDiscovery is explicit, the changed integration-style test proves the launch config no longer includes the user root, and the measured runtime behavior identifies duplicate system-message content.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem cache hits, runtime prompt reconstruction frequency, tokenization cost, and latency per model provider are not available in the repository, but the prior duplicate source and doubled system-message content are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. This PR removes repeated filesystem/prompt work and duplicate prompt bytes while preserving multi-root workspace instruction loading; the fix was recorded for regression learning.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publish customization updates or recompute the current plugin snapshot after discovery/agent changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Watcher-driven discovery updates publish customization state; currentAppliedPlugins or getAppliedPlugins then traverses discovered directories and children to build an in-memory plugin snapshot. The added path join and isEqualOrParent predicate execute during this projection and do not cross an external boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU scales linearly with discovered customization children, as it did before. The diff adds one path comparison per rule while eliminating user rules from downstream SDK directory conversion and runtime loading.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Watcher bursts are coalesced by the existing discovery refresh delayer. Snapshot projection is synchronous per caller; async settled snapshots await existing sync/discovery tasks concurrently. No new task fan-out or limiter change is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered customization arrays remain cached on the anchor. The projection itself is rebuilt as before; the added comparison has no independent cache and performs one URI ancestry check only for rule children. There is no negative-cache change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed operations are visible in the synchronous projection loop and existing callers are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of discovered rule files is not bounded here, but URI parsing already occurred for every projected rule before the diff and the added ancestry comparison is small relative to discovery and SDK loading.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The small O(number of rules) in-memory predicate does not change asymptotic projection cost and is offset by removing downstream duplicate boundary work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The production change is a targeted repeated-work fix: it removes runtime-owned user instructions from explicit SDK directories without adding expensive boundaries, unbounded state, concurrency bursts, or hot-path I/O. No performance finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
